Consequence: a body line of a selected multiline command is never itself offered to getCandidate, whichever command group (sprites included) is registered later or earlier. Registration order only decides between commands that accept the same start line.

crates/rustuml-parser/src/preprocess/mod.rs (!startsub): the collected body is also processed in place, except inside a !theme body expansion (whose sub blocks are already replayed into theme_tail) and the existing seed pass
invariant: A line that Java's getCandidate never offers as a command start (the body or END of a multiline command selected earlier) is never offered to the sprite group; a line owned by a sprite command reaches it with Java's text (no Rust-only comment stripping); a !startsub body takes part in the diagram where it is written.
causal_divergence: Round 2 offered every line a family parser did not otherwise claim to the sprite group, but the Rust family parsers do not model all of Java's multiline commands (multiline header/footer/caption in description, state and object; [ ... ] element bodies; legacy-activity note bodies), so body text such as 'Sprite sheets are loaded' became CommandSpriteFile. Separately, the preprocessor's Rust-only trailing-apostrophe stripping only spared the SVG start line, and !startsub bodies were never emitted in place (masked earlier by the in-TIM sprite collector).
planned_change: Port getCandidate's ownership rule per factory as a registry walk; gate the sprite dispatch on it. Exempt sprite start lines and open sprite command lines from the inline-comment stripping. Replay !startsub bodies in place outside theme expansion.
known_residue_planned: Single-line commands are modelled only where they can accept a start line of a later modelled multiline command (the addTitleCommands singles, CommandCreateElementFull, CommandCreateElementFull2); the other singles are disjoint by leading keyword or required token, argued per factory in the module.

ColorParser PART2's negative lookahead (?![\w;:.]) has no Rust regex equivalent. Every modelled grammar follows the colour leaf with end of line, whitespace, '{', '[', '#' or 'as'; for all but the last the lookahead-free form accepts the same lines, and the 'as' case needs a composite colour glued to 'as'.
FoxSignature prefilters are not applied in the walk (they only differ from the regex on a vertical-tab separator).
JSON validity in CommandCreateJson#finalVerification uses serde_json, not net.sourceforge.plantuml.json.JsonParser.

The comment exemption is tracked in the streaming preprocessor, so a sprite opened outside a procedure body and closed inside it is still stripped when the body is defined; unclosed sprite starts keep the exemption to end of file (Java strips nothing, and Java rejects such inputs).
